children: Asian markets were mostly lower on Monday on rising oil prices after Saudi Arabia shut a key pipeline following drone attacks and postponed talks with Gulf states. Hotter-than-expected US inflation data strengthened the case for a Federal Reserve rate hike.
U.S. stock futures were lower on Monday, with Dow futures down 0.11%, S&P 500 futures falling 0.49% and Nasdaq futures declining 1.26%.
In the U.S. on Friday, the Dow rose 0.98%, the S&P 500 gained 0.86% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.96%.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 1.06%, hitting a six-week low. Japan’s 10-year government bond yield held around 2.98% on Monday, remaining near its highest level in three decades. The Japanese yen eased toward 154 per dollar.
China’s Shanghai Composite gained 0.16%. Sentiment toward AI sector deteriorated after several major AI firms called for a slowdown in the technology's development.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index rose 0.38%, extending losses for a fourth straight session as investors remained cautious.
Australia's ASX remained almost flat after four straight sessions of losses.

title: Asian markets mostly lower as U.S. futures slide, oil prices rise
